name: Scope
text: Creative owns merging the *Science of Sleep Optimization* transcript into the AI Executive Assistant pattern immediately, using a live 10-minute Engineering ingest review to flag missing speaker/timestamp fields *before* the merge happens. This trades upfront debate for a fast, testable outcome—we’ll catch errors where they matter (in the AI’s output) instead of debating specs that may never be used again. Engineering’s live review keeps the process lightweight but accountable, while Creative moves the project forward without waiting for a perfect spec.

name: Scriv
text: The live 10-minute ingest review punts the problem to Engineering without fixing Creative’s core failure: they’re merging a transcript they didn’t validate. The real risk is that Engineering catches errors *after* Creative’s work is baked into the AI Assistant, making fixes costly. Instead, Creative should own a *post-merge* 10-minute sanity check—spot-check speaker/timestamp accuracy *before* the transcript hits the pipeline—then Engineering does a final ingest review. Settle it by running a pilot: Creative merges one transcript, does the sanity check, and Engineering measures how many errors slip through.

name: Reel
text: Creative owns merging the *Science of Sleep Optimization* transcript into the AI Executive Assistant pattern immediately, using a live 10-minute Engineering ingest review to flag missing fields or timestamps *before* the transcript hits production. This cuts the debate over static specs and lets us test the pattern’s robustness now instead of waiting for a perfect spec. The trade-off is accepting a small risk of minor errors slipping through—because a live review catches most issues fast, and perfection isn’t worth a week of delay.

name: Scriv
text: The live 10-minute ingest review punts the problem to Engineering without fixing the transcript’s speaker/timestamp gaps—those errors won’t vanish just because someone checks them faster. Better: Creative owns a *single* rule—timestamp every speaker change—and Engineering owns a 10-minute *automated* scan to flag violations before merge. Settle it by running the transcript through the scan; if it flags errors, Creative fixes them immediately.

name: Chisel
text: Creative owns a *live* 10-minute ingest review for the *Science of Sleep Optimization* transcript, flagging missing speaker/timestamp fields in real time before merging. This trades upfront debate for immediate, actionable quality control—no shelfware specs, no week-long delays. Engineering’s role shifts to validating the review’s output, not owning the checklist. The artifact is the reviewed transcript itself, ready for the AI Executive Assistant pattern.

name: Sift
text: The live 10-minute ingest review is a band-aid—it treats symptoms, not the disease. The real risk is that Engineering becomes the bottleneck every time Creative edits the transcript, turning a one-off into a recurring chore. Instead, Creative should own a *version-controlled* one-page spec that auto-validates against the transcript in real time, with Engineering only reviewing exceptions. That settles it: the artifact is a GitHub Action that flags drift, not a checklist that slows everyone down.
